recipes.name: Run 1
dims: Wedge (1/8 of a log), from a 12 in log
Length along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face
Length along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face
1.43 in at the bark, to sit flush

steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 85.06 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk. It is longer than a 72 in stick: splice two, or cut it from a longer log.

steps.title: Rip it flush
steps.text: This piece stands taller than the frame. Rip 1.43 in off the bark side, parallel to the stick's length, so it sits flush with both faces of the panel. Lay it on a sawn face on the bandsaw or table saw; tilt the blade 22.50° (half the slice's angle) so the cut runs square to the slice's centre line.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the RIGHT. Bevel 11.2° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 2.91 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face, down to 0.50 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 11.2° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Measure from the first cut and mark: 79.86 in along the point; 84.31 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 79.49 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the ripped face -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is only a sliver. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 84.31 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face, 79.86 in along the point, 79.49 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 1: standing on its point, bark toward the open side.

steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 84.70 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk. It is longer than a 72 in stick: splice two, or cut it from a longer log.

steps.title: Rip it flush
steps.text: This piece stands taller than the frame. Rip 1.43 in off the bark side, parallel to the stick's length, so it sits flush with both faces of the panel. Lay it on a sawn face on the bandsaw or table saw; tilt the blade 22.50° (half the slice's angle) so the cut runs square to the slice's centre line.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 30.0° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the RIGHT. Bevel 9.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 2.53 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face, down to 0.50 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Measure from the first cut and mark: 80.36 in along the point; 83.95 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 79.89 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the ripped face -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is only a sliver. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 83.95 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face, 80.36 in along the point, 79.89 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 1: standing on its point, bark toward the open side.

80 ends: mitre 30.0°, bevel 9.0° -- the panel's long edge; bevel half the 18.0° seam fold

Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.
